title: Route Change Conflict with Veteran Driver
brief: Handle a frustrated veteran delivery driver whose preferred run was reassigned due to emergency fleet maintenance.

edge.scenario: It is 5:30 AM in the dispatch office of a regional freight carrier. Two refrigerated trailers failed morning brake inspections, forcing dispatch to merge routes and assign senior drivers to unfamiliar, grueling inner-city runs. Jim storm into the dispatch booth holding his run sheet, visibly angry about losing his steady highway route.
edge.personaPublic: Jim is a 15-year veteran driver who expects predictability and seniority perks on the daily board. He is standing at your dispatch window holding his manifest with a hard, defensive posture.
edge.personaHidden: He is nursing a flare-up of chronic sciatica that makes stop-and-go city deliveries agonizing, but he is terrified to report it to company health. He feels disrespected that a younger dispatcher swapped his route without calling him first.
edge.goal: De-escalate Jim's anger, uncover his physical limitation, and agree on a feasible delivery run or assistance plan that keeps freight moving safely.

criteria.text: Acknowledges the frustration of a last-minute schedule change without being defensive.
Explains the operational breakdown clearly without blaming mechanics or management.
Asks an open question to uncover why this specific change is a problem today.
keywords: how can we make this work

criteria.text: Explores realistic adjustments without making impossible schedule promises.
Confirms an agreed run schedule and departure time before Jim walks away.

edge.opening: Fifteen years here, and you throw me on Route 14 downtown with twelve pallet drops? I took the southern highway run when the board opened yesterday. You don't just yank a senior guy's ticket at dawn and hand him a nightmare run without even talking to me first. I'm not taking that truck.
